title: Field Types and Database Mapping
description: Understand Prisma scalar types, optionality, lists, and native database type mappings with `@db` annotations.

data.text: Prisma provides standard scalar types (`String`, `Boolean`, `Int`, `BigInt`, `Float`, `Decimal`, `DateTime`, `Json`, `Bytes`) that translate seamlessly to TypeScript types. However, relational engines like PostgreSQL support dozens of specialized column types (e.g. `VARCHAR(100)`, `TEXT`, `TIMESTAMPTZ`, `UUID`, `JSONB`). Prisma uses native type attributes (`@db.*`) to give you fine-grained control over the physical schema.
Type Mapping Matrix: Prisma -> TypeScript -> PostgreSQL
A field is made optional (nullable) by appending a question mark `?`. In PostgreSQL, this maps to a column without the `NOT NULL` constraint. Appending `[]` indicates a list/array of items.

data.title: Native Type Customization in Practice
data.content: Using UUIDs, constrained text, precise currency, and PostgreSQL arrays in schema.prisma.
data.code:
model Product {
  id          String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  sku         String   @unique @db.VarChar(50)
  title       String   @db.VarChar(200)
  description String?  @db.Text
  price       Decimal  @db.Decimal(10, 2) // Max 99,999,999.99
  tags        String[] // PostgreSQL text[] native array
  metadata    Json?    @db.JsonB
  releasedAt  DateTime @db.Timestamptz(6)
}

data.title: Precision Warning: Float vs Decimal
data.text: Never use `Float` for money or financial balances! `Float` is a binary floating-point representation that suffers from rounding inaccuracies (e.g. 0.1 + 0.2 !== 0.3). Always use `Decimal` with `@db.Decimal(precision, scale)` for monetary values.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Prisma scalar types map to idiomatic TypeScript types automatically.
Use `@db.*` attributes to enforce strict database storage types like `VARCHAR` and `UUID`.
Always use `Decimal` for currency and financial calculations.
PostgreSQL native arrays (`String[]`) are supported directly by Prisma.
